title: Kernel roster: arch-and-length-aware sampler + proactive warmstart
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight kernel 'roster' subsystem that maintains a small ranked set of candidate kernels per model+hardware profile and sequence-length bucket. The roster will proactively warmstart KV/cache and pipeline micro-probes for top candidates during prefill spikes so the runtime can switch with minimal tail impact. Goals: (1) reduce 95th/99th tail latency for mixed-prefill/decode workloads; (2) improve average throughput for heterogeneous fleets (A100/V100/H100) with minimal overhead; (3) provide a low-cost online exploration budget that avoids destabilizing production SLA. Deliverables: roster data structures and API, sampling scheduler, warmstart probe runner, profiling telemetry hooks, rollout plan with canary/kill-switch, evaluation dashboards and a guidance doc for operator tuning.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Asha Patel: Created ticket. Sketch of roster idea in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Roster+Design. Initial questions about memory overhead for storing microprofiles across thousands of models.

2026-03-11 — Diego Morales: PoC for roster data structure implemented. Uses fixed-size LRU per (model,arch,seqlen-bucket) with lightweight aggregate stats (p95, p50, tokens/sec). Memory: ~120KB per 1k entries. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421.

2026-03-12 — Performance spikes: microbench on A100 shows roster warmstart produced 1.18x throughput at seq_len=64 under mixed prefill workload vs static kernel selector. Tail p99 reduced from 310ms to 260ms in 95th percentile experiments. Notes: cost of warmstart probes ~0.6% additional GPU cycles; acceptable for P1.

2026-03-13 — Diego Morales: Updated prototype to include probe backoff and probe budget per GPU. Added opt-in flags in config. Draft guidance added to Confluence: warmstart budget defaults and suggested values for Dedicated customers.
